from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

outline.topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers
outline.target_audience: University students with a foundational understanding of machine learning and neural networks.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Vector Embeddings
sections.content: Briefly explain that MLPs don't store text like a database; they store 'concepts' as coordinates in high-dimensional space. Visualize this as a library where similar facts are clustered together.
sections.example: Represent 'Cat' as a point [0.9, 0.1] and 'Dog' as [0.1, 0.9] on a 2D coordinate plane.

sections.title: The Anatomy of an MLP: Key-Value Pairs
sections.content: Explain that an MLP block in a Transformer acts as a 'key-value memory.' The first linear layer acts as a 'pattern matcher' (Key), and the second layer projects the result back to the vocabulary space (Value).
sections.example: Input: 'The capital of France is...' -> Pattern Matcher activates the 'France' neuron -> Value projector outputs 'Paris'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Nonlinear Activation as a Switch
sections.content: Introduce the ReLU or GeLU activation function. Explain it as a gate that only fires if the input matches a specific stored pattern, ensuring that factual storage is sparse and modular.
sections.example: Visual animation: A 'neuron' gate remains closed (0) until the input vector crosses a specific threshold, then snaps open to inject the factual information 'Paris'.

sections.title: Dynamic Synthesis: From Weights to Facts
sections.content: Explain that a single fact is not stored in one neuron, but distributed across the weights of the entire MLP layer, acting like a holographic image.
sections.example: If the model learns 'The sky is blue,' it modifies weights across multiple layers. If you 'mute' one neuron, the fact remains; mute the whole layer, and the fact disappears.

sections.title: Application: Editing the Model’s Knowledge
sections.content: Summarize how researchers can perform 'Model Editing' by surgically altering the specific weights in an MLP layer to update an outdated fact without retraining the whole network.
sections.example: Updating a model that thinks 'The President of the USA is X' by mathematically shifting the weights associated with that specific MLP layer to point to 'Y' instead.
